channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: AI Development Adds Vulnerability Noise, Calls for Resilience
item.description: AI-driven development increases software supply-chain complexity, flooding security teams with low-risk vulnerabilities. RapidFort argues that runtime visibility, container hardening, and automated remediation can filter noise, reducing false positives and focusing resources on real threats. Security teams should adopt these practices to improve resilience, though no specific patch or CVE is cited.

item.title: CISA Alerts on Exploited N-Able Email Bug
item.description: CISA warns that a vulnerability in N-Able’s email security platform has been exploited, threatening government departments. The flaw, identified as CVE-2026-134624, allows attackers to bypass spam and malware filtering, potentially delivering malicious content to users. N-Able has released a patch; agencies must update before Thanksgiving to mitigate the critical risk.

item.title: EU Academy Data Exposed in AI-Assisted Attack
item.description: The European Commission discovered that an AI-assisted cyberattack exposed names and email addresses of EU Academy users. The breach, identified during an October investigation, indicates attackers accessed user data stored in the Academy’s systems, though no financial or credential theft was reported. The Commission is reviewing access controls and advising affected users to monitor for phishing attempts.

item.title: Chrome Vulnerability Affects Versions Before 158.0.8127.88
item.description: Google issued a security advisory for a vulnerability affecting Chrome versions prior to 158.0.8127.88 on Windows/Mac and 158.0.8127.88 on Linux. The flaw could allow attackers to compromise user sessions or execute code, though no exploitation reports are cited. Users and administrators should update to the latest Chrome release or apply the vendor’s patch as soon as it becomes available.

item.title: Volant Manticore: Flying Under the Radar
item.description: Key Points Introduction Check Point Research is tracking a previously undocumented Iran-nexus threat group who we named Volant Manticore. What started in July 2026 as a single backdoor delivered to a Cyprus-based airline through a fake CV has since expanded into a broader cluster of activity that we traced back to September 2025.

item.title: Critical VMware ESX Flaws Let Remote Attackers Execute Malicious Code on Virtualization Hosts
item.description: Broadcom has disclosed 23 VMware vulnerabilities, including two critical flaws that could let attackers run code directly on ESX hosts and a third that could let them access vCenter without signing in. The Broadcom security advisory, VMSA-2026-0011, was published on November 24. It says the flaws were privately reported and does not report active exploitation.

item.title: McDonald's Japan Exposes App User Location Data
item.description: A data breach at McDonald's Japan exposed a database of official smartphone app users, revealing their location information. Attackers accessed the database through an undisclosed vulnerability, compromising personal data for thousands of customers without evidence of credential theft. McDonald's Japan has notified affected users and is working with security teams to investigate the breach and strengthen database access controls.

item.title: GTA 6 Hacker Sentenced, Released Same Day
item.description: A former Lapsus$ member, Arion Kurtaj, was sentenced to seven years for leaking Grand Theft Auto VI footage after a guilty plea. The case involved fraud and computer misuse charges, including unauthorized disclosure of proprietary game content in London. Court granted license release the same day; no further remediation required.

item.title: Hackers Deploy ZQAgent Backdoor to Run Malicious Commands and Access Files on Linux Servers
item.description: A new Linux backdoor called ZQAgent is giving attackers a long-term foothold on compromised servers. It can run commands, move through folders, read files and open network tunnels. The malware was dropped by ARTEX, an AI-driven hacking framework.

item.title: Shirudo AI Tool Protects Unpatched Linux Systems
item.description: OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, an open-source Linux security tool that deploys temporary runtime protections to block exploitation of unpatched vulnerabilities. Shirudo leverages AI-driven heuristics to detect and mitigate exploitation attempts against known CVEs without requiring service restarts, addressing the gap before patch deployment. Administrators can deploy Shirudo immediately to shield systems, then apply official patches once available.

item.title: VMware vCenter Hit by Another Critical 9.8-Rated Auth Bypass Flaw After Zero-Day Exploitation
item.description: Broadcom has shipped patches to address 23 vulnerabilities impacting VMware ESX, vCenter, Workstation, Fusion, and Avi Load Balancer, including one critical bug that could be abused to bypass authentication. The critical vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-123903, is rated 9.8 out of 10.0 on the CVSS scoring system. It resides in the VMware Directory Service ("vmdir").

item.title: Codesys Visualization Vulnerabilities Pre-4.11.0.0 Advisory
item.description: The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security issued advisory AV26-1199, warning that Codesys Visualization versions prior to 4.11.0.0 contain multiple vulnerabilities. These flaws could allow attackers to gain unauthorized access or execute arbitrary code within the visualization component, potentially compromising industrial control systems. Users should review the provided links and apply available updates or workarounds as soon as patches are released.

item.title: Wiz Enhances OpenAI Daybreak Defense with Security Intelligence
item.description: Wiz Research announced integration of its cloud security intelligence into OpenAI's Daybreak Defense Factory, aiming to improve AI-driven vulnerability analysis. The integration leverages Wiz's data feeds to identify code remediation opportunities, but no specific vulnerability is disclosed. OpenAI can now apply Wiz insights to prioritize patching and reduce exposure to emerging threats.

item.title: McDonald’s Japan Breach Reveals Purchase and Location Data
item.description: McDonald’s Japan announced a cybersecurity breach that exposed customers’ purchase histories and mobile device location data. The incident involved unauthorized access to the company’s customer database, potentially compromising sensitive personal information for a large user base. The company is investigating the breach and has notified affected customers, while security teams should monitor for phishing or credential misuse.

item.title: SUSE Advises NeuVector Stack Buffer Overflow Vulnerabilities
item.description: SUSE reports stack buffer overflow vulnerabilities in NeuVector dataplane affecting versions prior to 5.7.0, 5.5.6, and 5.6.5, triggered by DLP/WAF rule limits. The 2048-byte overflow can corrupt memory and cause denial-of-service, but no remote code execution or active exploitation has been confirmed. Users should apply the SUSE update or upgrade NeuVector to a newer release to mitigate the DoS risk.

item.title: CVE-2026-131914 Enables Unauthenticated ASP.NET RCE
item.description: Attackers exploited CVE-2026-131914, a critical flaw in Idunno AntiCsrf used by ASP.NET WebForms, to trigger web redirects and confirm exploitation. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote code execution with a CVSS score of 9.8, and threat actors have actively leveraged it. Microsoft and vendors have released patches; administrators should update the AntiCsrf library and disable redirects until the fix is applied.

item.title: Bedrock Data Launches Intent-Aware AI Agent DLP
item.description: Bedrock Data launched Agent DLP, a runtime data loss prevention tool that infers user intent and evaluates AI agent actions against policy. The tool weighs intent and behavior, enabling continued AI agent use while protecting sensitive data across tool and LLM calls. It also supports off-the-shelf integrations and offers a policy enforcement framework for AI workflows.

item.title: Elastic Deploys AI Agents to Triage SOC Alerts
item.description: Elastic Security 9.6 introduces AlertZero, AI agents that triage alerts, hunt threats, and tune detection rules. The release adds Linux ransomware protection, expands entity resolution, and adds 143 detection rules for AI agents and LLM platforms. AlertZero groups workers into four watches-triage, threat hunting, detection engineering, and others-to automate SOC backlog.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Thunderbird Update for Important Vulnerabilities
item.description: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.6 receives a security update for Thunderbird, addressing several important vulnerabilities. The advisory references multiple CVEs with CVSS base scores, indicating potential remote code execution or privilege escalation if unpatched. Users should apply the update immediately to mitigate the risk, as the patch resolves all identified flaws.

item.title: RHEL 10 cifs-utils Update Released
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for cifs-utils on RHEL 10, fixing vulnerabilities that could enable remote code execution via SMB. Each flaw carries a CVSS base score, but the advisory lists no specific CVE identifiers. Apply the patch through standard RHEL update channels immediately; no configuration changes are required.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Critical Ruby 3.3 Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a critical security update for the ruby:3.3 module on RHEL9, addressing multiple vulnerabilities. The update mitigates high-severity flaws, each with a CVSS base score detailed in the referenced CVE links, though no active exploitation has been reported. Administrators should apply the ruby:3.3 update immediately to prevent potential denial-of-service or privilege escalation attacks.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Important LibreOffice Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released an important security update for LibreOffice on RHEL9.6 Extended Update Support, addressing several vulnerabilities. Each flaw carries a CVSS base score listed in the CVE references, though no active exploitation has been documented. Users should install the LibreOffice update promptly to mitigate potential denial-of-service or privilege escalation risks.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102905: Important: container-tools:rhel8 security update
item.description: An update for the container-tools:rhel8 module is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.6 Advanced Mission Critical Update Support and Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.6 Extended Update Support Long-Life Add-On. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important.

item.title: Infrastructure Vulnerabilities Highlight Systemic Fragility
item.description: Schneier's essay examines how America’s critical infrastructure remains fragile due to aging systems, piecemeal patching, and hobbyist maintenance. The author argues that centralization and incremental upgrades create a single point of failure, causing widespread outages when components fail. The piece calls for systemic investment and coordinated security practices to reduce the risk of cascading infrastructure breakdowns.

item.title: Azure API Management flaw used to steal credentials
item.description: Microsoft warned that a vulnerability in Azure API Management (APIM) was exploited to exfiltrate credentials from customers’ instances, affecting Norwegian energy firms and others. The flaw in APIM Classic tiers lets attackers bypass authentication and retrieve stored secrets, potentially compromising downstream services. Microsoft recommends applying the latest APIM patch, disabling Classic tiers, and rotating exposed credentials immediately.

item.title: Google Researcher Exposes .NET Bit-Flip Code Integrity Bypass
item.description: A Google Project Zero researcher demonstrated that a single bit flip in .NET files bypasses Windows code integrity, allowing local attackers to run untrusted code. The flaw also bypassed VirtualBox process hardening on Windows and is tracked as CVE-2026-87268, exposing local privilege escalation. Administrators should update .NET Framework to the latest patch or apply vendor mitigations to prevent exploitation.

item.title: KEPCO Data Breach Exposes 1.5 Million Personal Records
item.description: Hackers accessed KEPCO’s customer portal and supplier relationship management platform, exfiltrating personal data of approximately 1.5 million users. The breach involved names, contact details, and possibly financial identifiers, though the full data scope is unclear. KEPCO has not yet released a detailed incident response plan; affected parties should monitor for identity theft and consider credit monitoring services.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102920: Important: thunderbird security, bug fix, and enhancement update
item.description: An update for thunderbird is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.4 Advanced Mission Critical Update Support and Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.4 Extended Update Support Long-Life Add-On. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Critical Ruby 3.3 Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a critical update for the ruby:3.3 module on Enterprise Linux 8, fixing several security bugs. The patch addresses high-severity flaws that could enable remote code execution or privilege escalation, with CVSS scores up to 9.2. Administrators should apply RHSA-2026:102909 immediately and confirm the Ruby runtime is at the patched version.

item.title: EvilTokens Phishing Persists After Microsoft Takedown
item.description: Despite Microsoft shutting down the EvilTokens phishing-as-a-service kit, attackers continue to deploy new phishing hosts targeting Microsoft 365 accounts. The campaign exploits social engineering to trick users into revealing credentials, potentially granting attackers full access to corporate Microsoft 365 environments. Security teams should enforce multi-factor authentication, monitor for anomalous sign-ins, and educate users about phishing indicators.

item.title: LibreOffice Vulnerabilities Patched in RHEL 9.4 SAP
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for LibreOffice on RHEL 9.4 Update Services for SAP Solutions, addressing multiple vulnerabilities. The update carries an Important impact rating, with CVSS base scores available via CVE references, but no active exploitation has been reported. Administrators should apply the latest LibreOffice package to mitigate the identified risks.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Critical Update for ruby:4.0
item.description: A critical flaw in the ruby:4.0 module for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 triggered an urgent security update. The vulnerability, rated with a high CVSS score, permits remote code execution via the Ruby interpreter and is linked to several CVEs. Red Hat released the patch in RHSA-2026-102883; users must apply it immediately to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Researchers Plant Secrets in AI Prompts; Attackers Discover Them
item.description: Researchers embedded Amazon access keys into AI prompt templates, which attackers later located and tested against AWS accounts. The key leakage exploited prompt injection, enabling attackers to validate credentials in real time; no confirmed account takeover was reported. Affected organizations should rotate exposed keys, audit prompt usage, and enforce strict secrets management to mitigate future leaks.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102908: Important: libXi security update
item.description: An update for libXi is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7 Extended Lifecycle Support. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102516: Moderate: firewalld security update
item.description: An update for firewalld is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Moderate. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Important Update for Container Tool Suite
item.description: Red Hat issued a security update for buildah, conmon, containernetworking-plugins, containers-common, fuse-overlayfs, gvisor-tap-vsock, oci-seccomp-bpf-hook, podman, runc, skopeo, and slirp4netns on Enterprise Linux 9.6 EUS. The update addresses multiple vulnerabilities with CVSS scores in the Important range, mitigating potential container escape or privilege escalation risks. Administrators should apply the RHSA-2026:102529 package updates immediately to secure container runtimes and associated networking components.

item.title: Red Hat Releases cifs-utils Patch for RHEL 9.8
item.description: Red Hat issued a cifs-utils update for RHEL 9.8 EUS, fixing vulnerabilities that could enable remote code execution via SMB. Each flaw is linked to a CVE and carries a CVSS base score, with Red Hat rating the issue as Important. Apply the patch or upgrade to the latest RHEL 9.8 release to eliminate the risk.

item.title: MFA Bypassed via Phone Scams Targeting Microsoft 365
item.description: Cybercriminals posing as corporate IT support trick employees into revealing Microsoft 365 credentials, bypassing MFA to access OneDrive and SharePoint. They exfiltrated emails and files from compromised accounts and demanded ransom via Teams or email, exploiting social engineering. Teams should enforce verification protocols, monitor anomalous activity, and restrict external sharing to mitigate similar attacks.

item.title: Microsoft Patches Azure API Management Flaw Targeting Secrets
item.description: Microsoft discovered a flaw in Azure API Management Classic that allowed attackers to search for access tokens and secrets. The vulnerability, enabling credential theft and unauthorized API access, was reported by Norway's National Security Authority and is actively exploited. Microsoft released a patch in the latest update; customers should apply it immediately and audit API permissions to mitigate risk.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102514: Important: buildah, conmon, container-selinux, containers-common, criu, fuse-overlayfs, gvisor-tap-vsock, oci-seccomp-bpf-hook, podman, skopeo, and slirp4netns security, bug fix, and enhancement update
item.description: An update for buildah, conmon, container-selinux, containers-common, criu, fuse-overlayfs, gvisor-tap-vsock, oci-seccomp-bpf-hook, podman, skopeo, and slirp4netns is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.0 Extended Update Support. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important.

item.title: Elecbrakes Bluetooth Flaws Enable Forced Trailer Braking
item.description: Critical Bluetooth vulnerabilities in Elecbrakes trailer controllers allow nearby attackers to force braking, potentially causing accidents. The flaw exploits insecure Bluetooth pairing and command authentication, enabling remote manipulation of braking systems without user interaction. Manufacturers should update firmware to patch the vulnerabilities and disable unused Bluetooth interfaces to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Red Hat Issues container-tools:rhel8 Security Update for RHEL 8.4
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the container-tools:rhel8 module on RHEL 8.4 AMCS and EUS LLA, addressing multiple vulnerabilities. The update contains fixes for issues with CVSS scores listed in the CVE references, but no active exploitation has been reported. Red Hat recommends applying the patch through the standard RHEL update channels to mitigate potential remote code execution.

item.title: Peninsula Energy Halts Trading After Mine Cyber Incident
item.description: Peninsula Energy reported a cybersecurity incident at its Wyoming uranium project, temporarily disrupting operations and prompting a trading halt. The breach details remain undisclosed, but the company indicated that critical operational systems were impacted, raising concerns over supply chain continuity. Peninsula Energy is coordinating with cybersecurity teams and regulators to assess the incident and resume trading.

item.title: CISA Flags Exploited VMware, SAP, Cisco, Apache Flaws
item.description: CISA added four exploited vulnerabilities affecting VMware vCenter, SAP NetWeaver, Cisco Expressway, and Apache Roller to its KEV catalog. All four flaws were actively exploited in the wild, prompting CISA to urge federal civilian agencies to patch by November 23. Administrators should apply vendor patches or workarounds immediately to mitigate the exploitation risk.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102880: Important: ImageMagick security update
item.description: An update for ImageMagick is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7 Extended Lifecycle Support. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: GlobeTopper faces up to $2.5 million in lost revenue after hackers steal $70,000 in gift cards
item.description: According to a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), parent company iQSTEL said GlobeTopper detected the intrusion on October 22 and took the platform offline the next morning after spotting further unauthorized activity.

item.title: Suzlon Reports Cyber Incident, No Impact on Critical Systems
item.description: Suzlon Energy disclosed a cyber incident on November 23, 2026, claiming no disruption to its wind turbine control or business-critical applications. The company activated incident response procedures, limited potential impact, and notified Indian regulatory authorities, indicating containment of the event. Stakeholders should review Suzlon’s incident response documentation and ensure continued monitoring of operational technology networks.

item.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Ship for GitHub PR Review
item.description: Anthropic released Claude Ship in beta, letting Claude Code review GitHub pull requests, push fixes, and approve changes when policy allows. The tool does not merge code automatically; repository permissions and branch rules still govern integration. Security teams can use Claude Ship to automate reviews, but must enforce branch protection and review policies to retain control.

item.title: Windows Remote Access API Vulnerability Enables SYSTEM Privilege Escalation
item.description: A flaw in the Windows Remote Access API lets an attacker with limited local access run code with SYSTEM privileges. Microsoft assigned CVE-2026-119853 a CVSS score of 7.8 and rated the issue Important, but no active exploitation has been reported. Microsoft released a patch on Patch Tuesday; teams should apply it immediately via Windows Update or WSUS.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102854: Critical: ruby security update
item.description: An update for ruby is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Critical. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.
